summary_hint: <Permit type> permit #<number> from <jurisdiction> for <property address>, status <status>, issued <issue date>; <type of work> at $<estimated cost>.

typed_core.name: issuing_jurisdiction_or_department
typed_core.why: identity/source — which authority issued the permit

typed_core.name: permit_number
typed_core.prompt_hint: Capture the jurisdiction and permit number verbatim for independent lookup.

typed_core.name: parent_job_or_plan_number
typed_core.why: disambiguator — links sub-permits to a parent job/plan

typed_core.name: property_address
typed_core.why: identity/linkage — the job/property; must match subject (flattened from address)

typed_core.name: parcel_or_tax_map_number
typed_core.why: identity — parcel key for property matching

typed_core.name: owner_name
typed_core.why: identity — the property owner (flattened from owner_name_and_address object)

typed_core.name: owner_address
typed_core.why: disambiguator — owner mailing address vs job address (flattened from object)

typed_core.name: project_description
typed_core.why: processor — scope of work a reviewer reads

typed_core.name: estimated_construction_cost
typed_core.why: processor — scale of work (money stays string)

typed_core.name: final_or_close_date
typed_core.why: processor — whether the permit was finaled/closed

typed_core.name: applicant_name
typed_core.why: identity — who pulled the permit (flattened from object)

nested_lists.name: inspection_results
nested_lists.shape_reason: chosen over required_inspections because results carry the pass/fail outcome a reviewer needs; the two overlap and one list fits the budget (flat-row + one source)

fields.name: type
fields.why: processor confirms permitted work passed — the kind of inspection

fields.name: result
fields.why: processor — the pass/fail outcome a reviewer needs

rejected.name: party_names / party_addresses
rejected.reason: generic; superseded by typed owner/applicant/contractor fields

rejected.name: loan_number
rejected.reason: rarely present on a municipal permit; no consumer here

rejected.name: contractor_license_numbers, required_inspections, open_violations_or_corrections
rejected.reason: candidate lists deferred — budget one list, zero rules

rejected.name: certificate_of_occupancy_or_completion
rejected.reason: narrative object; the close date + status capture the substance

encoding_variations: Permit status vocabulary varies by jurisdiction ('Finaled', 'Closed', 'C of O issued', 'Expired'); permit_status + final_or_close_date together disambiguate a genuinely completed permit from a lapsed one.
issue_date (permit identity) vs document_issue_date (generic) can collide — prefer the permit's own issue date; the generic field is rejected to avoid duplication.
Multiple dates (application/issue/final/expiration) all appear — keep them distinct; a reviewer reconstructs the timeline.

open_questions.q: Which inspection list — inspection_results (chosen) vs required_inspections. They overlap; results carry outcomes.
open_questions.recommendation: keep inspection_results; fold 'required' into it if a jurisdiction lists both. Flag if a rule ever needs the required-vs-performed gap

open_questions.q: Completion evidence — certificate_of_occupancy_or_completion is rejected in favor of status+close-date.
options: add certificate_of_occupancy_or_completion as its own typed field
open_questions.recommendation: confirm with the domain expert that C-of-O presence isn't needed as its own typed field for renovation loans

notes: No rules read this document today, so there is no rule floor; a building permit supports property condition / completed-work verification (renovation, ADU, post-repair).

Prompt hint (doc-level): this supports completed-work / property-condition verification — the reviewer wants correct property, work described, and evidence the permit reached final/closed status without open violations.
Prompt hint (doc-level): do not judge whether work is 'complete' — capture permit_status, final_or_close_date, and inspection results as stated.

PII: no personal SSN/account field in this catalog. owner_name/owner_address are property-owner identity at standard sensitivity — flag owner_address for review as a home address. loan_number (confidential) exists in the catalog but is rejected (rarely on a permit).
Ambiguity: permit_type's why is 'identity/processor' (classified identity, first listed).
